directAnswer: Pope St. John Paul II was Karol Wojtyła of Poland, the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, who reigned from 16 October 1978 to 2 April 2005, one of the longest pontificates in history. He traveled to more than 120 countries, helped inspire the peaceful end of communism in Eastern Europe, founded World Youth Day, promulgated the Catechism of the Catholic Church, and was canonized in 2014.

sections.h2: Karol Wojtyła: Actor, Laborer, Priest and Philosopher
paras: Karol Józef Wojtyła was born on 18 May 1920 in Wadowice, Poland. By the age of twenty he had lost his mother, his only brother and his father. During the Nazi occupation he worked in a quarry and a chemical plant, took part in an underground theater, and studied for the priesthood in a clandestine seminary in Kraków. He was ordained in 1946.

After doctoral studies in Rome and Poland he taught ethics at the Catholic University of Lublin and developed a philosophy of the human person. He became auxiliary bishop of Kraków in 1958, participated in the Second Vatican Council, and was named archbishop of Kraków in 1964 and a cardinal in 1967.

sections.h2: A Polish Pope and the Fall of Communism
paras: Elected on 16 October 1978 at 58, he was the first Polish pope and the first non-Italian since Adrian VI. His inaugural homily urged the world, Be not afraid. His first visit to Poland in June 1979 drew enormous crowds and is widely credited with helping to give rise to the Solidarity movement.

On 13 May 1981 he was shot in St. Peter's Square by Mehmet Ali Ağca and seriously wounded. He attributed his survival to Our Lady of Fatima, whose feast falls on that day, and later visited and forgave his attacker in prison. Historians broadly agree that his moral support for freedom in Poland contributed to the largely peaceful collapse of communist regimes in 1989.

sections.h2: Teaching: Encyclicals, the Catechism and the Theology of the Body
paras: John Paul II wrote fourteen encyclicals, among them Redemptor hominis (1979), Laborem exercens (1981), Centesimus annus (1991), Veritatis splendor (1993), Evangelium vitae (1995), in which he urged a culture of life, and Fides et ratio (1998). His Wednesday catechesis from 1979 to 1984 on human love became known as the Theology of the Body.

He promulgated the revised Code of Canon Law in 1983 and the Catechism of the Catholic Church in 1992. In 2002 he added the Luminous Mysteries to the Rosary, and in 2000 he established Divine Mercy Sunday for the universal Church.

sections.h2: World Youth Day and the Pilgrim Pope in America
paras: He made more than a hundred journeys abroad, visiting the United States several times, including his 1979 tour and his 1987 visit, and in 1993 he celebrated World Youth Day in Denver. He had established World Youth Day in the mid-1980s, and the gatherings drew millions of young people.

He also pursued dialogue with other Christians and other religions: he visited the synagogue of Rome in 1986, convened the World Day of Prayer for Peace in Assisi that year, and prayed at the Western Wall in Jerusalem during the Great Jubilee of 2000. He canonized and beatified more people than any earlier pope.

In his later years he lived publicly with Parkinson's disease, continuing his ministry as his strength declined. He died on 2 April 2005, the vigil of Divine Mercy Sunday. Benedict XVI beatified him on 1 May 2011, and Pope Francis canonized him on 27 April 2014. His memorial is celebrated on October 22, the anniversary of his papal inauguration.

keyFacts: Born Karol Wojtyła in Wadowice, Poland, on 18 May 1920
Survived an assassination attempt on 13 May 1981
Promulgated the 1983 Code of Canon Law and the 1992 Catechism
Established World Youth Day; hosted WYD Denver 1993
Canonized by Pope Francis on 27 April 2014; memorial October 22

faqs.question: What is the Theology of the Body?
faqs.answer: It is the name given to John Paul II's series of Wednesday audiences from 1979 to 1984 on the meaning of the human body, sexuality and marriage in God's plan, which has strongly influenced Catholic marriage preparation and catechesis.

faqs.question: How did John Paul II contribute to the fall of communism?
faqs.answer: His 1979 pilgrimage to Poland and steady defense of human rights and religious freedom encouraged the Solidarity movement and peaceful resistance, which historians see as a factor in the collapse of communist rule in 1989.

faqs.question: Why is his feast day October 22?
faqs.answer: October 22 is the anniversary of his papal inauguration Mass in 1978, at which he told the world, Be not afraid. The Church chose it for his memorial after his canonization in 2014.
